challenges.title: ERO rates, the night window and Sunday working

items.title: ERO minimum wage rises at the new year
items.text: The Employment Regulation Order of the Contract Cleaning Industry Joint Labour Committee (S.I. No. 430/2025) raises the minimum wage from €14.10 (from 17 October 2025) to €14.80 per hour from 1 January 2026.

items.title: Night allowance between midnight and 6am
items.text: The €1.00-per-hour allowance applies to work between 00:00 and 06:00, provided at least 3 hours are worked within that window — from 1 January 2026, that comes to €15.80 per hour.

items.title: Sunday working at double rate
items.text: Sunday work is paid at double the hourly rate — €29.60 per hour from 1 January 2026. With changing sites and teams, that's error-prone by hand.

solutions.title: How Klacks takes the load off facility services in Ireland
solutions.subtitle: From optimised routes to the correct ERO allowance — it all fits together.

items.title: Site routes optimised
items.text: Klacks sequences sites so that journeys stay short — whether by car, bike or on foot.

items.title: ERO minimum wage applied automatically
items.text: Klacks calculates using the current ERO rate of €14.80 per hour from 1 January 2026, and updates future increases centrally.

items.title: Night allowance within the right time window
items.text: The €1.00-per-hour night allowance between 00:00 and 06:00 is only correctly calculated where at least 3 hours are worked within that window — Klacks checks this automatically.

items.title: Sunday working recorded at double rate
items.text: Klacks automatically recognises Sunday shifts and applies the double hourly rate of €29.60 per hour (from 1 January 2026).

items.title: On-premise: data stays in-house
items.text: Klacks runs on your own infrastructure — staff data never leaves your organisation, not even for the AI.

items.title: Klacksy schedules by voice
items.text: "Schedule the sites in the North district for tomorrow morning" is enough — Klacksy optimises the route and team and factors in the ERO rates at the same time.
